column1: # Indonesia, Kemenag: 18 fitted kab/kota, myQuran's republication of bimasislam.kemenag.go.id
# (api.myquran.com/v2/sholat/jadwal/<id>/<yyyy>/<mm>): 2026, 2027 and 2028 are rows (myQuran answers 2024 too). When 2026
# was the only year held, no second year existed for a forward split, so each place's own 365-day file is split by date, forward in time:
# fit on Jan-Sep (273 days), test on Oct-Dec (92 days) — a better split than "no split at all", the
# only one profiles-tested.md ran. The 13 of the research round were fetched on 25 Sep 2026; the five
# kota the weekly monitor first met on 28 Sep 2026 (Medan, Palembang, Semarang, Surabaya, Yogyakarta)
# were fetched whole on 29 Sep 2026 from the same endpoint (ruling R104; their Sep-Oct rows equal the
# monitor's capture, archive/tables/monitor/id-kemenag/<kota>-2026.txt). For every place the Jan-Sep
# fit alone holds Oct-Dec; the registry's margins are fitted over both halves. Checked at each kab/kota's
# own unit (lat/lon empty). The monitor's 28 Sep 2026 recaptures of the 13 hold no day their files do
# not (identical on all 61 days), so they are not rows here.
# End of eating (audit of 3 Oct 2026, before Ramadan 1448): Kemenag's imsak (Subuh - 10) is a precaution these files do not hold;
# the fast begins at Subuh, so the Fajr column is also checked as the end of eating (F+E).
# 2027 (track T4, 11 Oct 2026): the weekly monitor first read Kemenag's 2027 on 5 Oct 2026; every place's 2027 table is a
# row below (the prove of 5 Oct 2026 added nine; the other nine were one minute early on 21 or 22 March 2027, and at
# Palembang's Asr on one day). Kemenag's tables lag a day's change on 21 and 22 March (its step at the
# equinox): the method now carries that step (DayRule.LAG_EQUINOX_KEMENAG) and every unit's margins are fitted over
# every 2026 and 2027 row alike (Kemenag.kt), so all of them are fit, Oct-Dec 2026 too, and none is held out.
# 2028 (review of track T4, 11 Oct 2026): myQuran answers 2028 already, for all eighteen (read with the monitor's own
# fetchers/kemenag.py code, the place-name check included; pinned under archive/tables/pinned/id-kemenag/2026-10-11/,

# the eighteen places, its step falls on 21 March alone (in 2024, the other leap year held, on 21 and 22 March as in
# 2026 and 2027), never on 20 March, so the rule's two dates cover it.
# The 2027 rows check the end of eating as the 2026 rows do (F+E): the prove rows of 5 Oct 2026 had taken the
# fetcher's F, which the fetcher now gives as F+E.
